carbon_policy_signal.item: COP31 draft text signals immediate fossil fuel transition commitment; EU Phase 2 ETS compliance tightens if binding.
carbon_policy_signal.why_it_matters: Binding coal phase-out language accelerates thermal displacement and raises EUA floor via stricter carbon budgets; supports fuel-switch margin compression in power generation.

freshness_caveat: Coal (8th-percentile) and Clean Dark spread are stale as of 2025-12-26 and 2025-12-31 respectively (320–325 days old); merit-order and thermal dispatch signals cannot be confirmed with current data. TTF, GB Power, Renewables, and EUA are fresh (0–3 days old).
risk_flags: Coal data stale (325 days old, as of 2025-12-26); latest 8th-percentile but no fresh signal for merit-order merit shifts this week.
Clean Dark also stale (320 days old); cannot confirm whether coal-gas spread has tightened since year-end.
GB Power -15.21% intraday yet still 93rd-percentile: indicates structural tightness not weather-driven; check grid constraints or capacity margin data.
EUA 2.1σ move lower despite COP31 bullish rhetoric suggests profit-taking or carbon-budget repricing; watch Phase 2 auction calendar (MSR intake sensitivity).

base.summary: COP31 final text moderate on immediacy; GB grid stabilizes; renewables mean-revert to 55–60%. TTF flat to +2%, power -5% from highs.

downside.summary: COP31 fossil language watered down; EU electrification softening confirmed; mild winter. EUA -6-10%, power -15-22%, coal repricing higher.

upside.summary: COP31 binding coal phase-out language + UK cold snap drives GB constraint tighter. EUA +8-12%, TTF +6-10%, power +12-18%.

themes: GB-DE power divergence: GB at decade highs amid tight GB-specific constraints
Arctic LNG exit narrows EU gas sources, lifts TTF curve risk premium
COP31 fossil-transition language vs. EU electrification softening creates policy asymmetry
Renewables at 87th-percentile (65% load share today) suppressing thermal dispatch
top_drivers: GB Power extremes (93rd-percentile, -15% intraday): grid constraint or demand anomaly signaling structural tightness, not weather-driven mean reversion.
Arctic LNG reroute to Asia (2027): eliminates Russian swing supply, narrows EU LNG optionality, props TTF seasonal curve and supports power baseload.
COP31 fossil-transition text vs. EU electrification softening: policy cross-current creating EUA repricing (down 1.91% despite bullish headlines) and coal displacement uncertainty.
top_takeaway: GB Power at 93rd-percentile, EUA selling off (-1.91%, 2.1σ) despite COP31 fossil-transition rhetoric; Arctic LNG reroute to Asia from 2027 tightens EU gas supply and supports power baseload.

watchlist.why: 93rd-percentile yet down 15% today and -12.25% weekly; constraint-driven or demand shock — if structural, supports premium longer-term.

watchlist.metric: TTF seasonal curve post-Arctic LNG reroute
watchlist.why: Russian LNG to Asia from 2027 narrows swing supply; monitor Q2 2027 forward spreads and LNG import routes (Atlantic swing availability).
If binding language on immediate coal phase-out, lifts coal displacement risk and EUA floor; if vague, EUA repricing lower likely continues.
65% load today (87th-percentile, +33% daily); if sustained >60% through winter, thermal baseload margins compress; watch daily intraday spread.
If COP31 final text waters down long-term clean-power targets, forward power curve risk premium deflates; bearish for Cal+2 and beyond.
